title: Why Experience Gifts Make the Best Holiday Gifts for Mental Health
summary: Why experience gifts may support mental health more than stuff, plus holiday experience gift ideas for couples, kids, parents, and any budget.
body_markdown:
An experience gift is a present the person lives through instead of keeps. Think of a cooking class, tickets to a show, a day hike, or a planned afternoon together. **** They’re **** often called experiential gifts or non-material gifts.


[Research](https://bpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/blogs.cornell.edu/dist/b/6819/files/2019/12/GilovichKumarJampol.2015.pdf) suggests that experiential purchases bring more happiness because they increase social relationships, form a bigger part of a person’s identity, and create less comparisons than material purchases.


**Experience Gifts Give People Something to Look Forward To**


The good feelings that come from an experience gift may begin long before the day itself.[Research published in Psychological Science](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614546556) found that people enjoyed waiting for an experience more than waiting for a material purchase.


That difference can matter most in the months with less daylight. When January feels long and gray, a concert ticket for February or a spring getaway can be a bright spot on the calendar. It’s something fun to count down to, especially for people who struggle with the[winter blues](https://lifestance.com/blog/the-winter-blues-could-it-be-seasonal-affective-disorder/) .


**Experience Gifts Bring People Closer**


An experience gift can do more than make someone happy. It can also bring individuals exchanging gifts closer. In[a study in the Journal of Consumer Research](https://doi.org/10.1093/jcr/ucw067) , people who received an experience felt a stronger bond with the giver than people who received a physical gift. This was true even when the giver didn’t come along. The researchers found that the bond grew from the feelings people had while enjoying the experience, not from the moment they opened the gift.


**Experience Gifts Tend to Stay With People Longer**


A new gadget or sweater is exciting at first, but over time, most people get used to it, and the thrill fades. Experiences can work differently. Instead of fading, a good memory often gets better with time. For instance, the rainy camping trip where everything went wrong slowly turns into the funniest story of the year. Experiences can also become part of who people are, and they give everyone involved something to laugh about and talk about for years to come.


**Less Focus on Stuff, Less Pressure**


Some objects carry real meaning, like the[comfort objects](https://lifestance.com/blog/psychological-benefits-comfort-objects/) many people hold onto for years. Still,[a large review of studies on materialism and well-being](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037409) found that people who put a high value on money and possessions tended to report lower well-being.


Giving an experience can gently shift the focus of the season away from what is under the tree and toward the time you spend together. It may also ease some of the[financial strain](https://lifestance.com/blog/holiday-stress-financial-strain/) of holiday shopping, because an experience can be planned around a budget, from a concert getaway to a homemade dinner and a movie night on the couch.
